description: Somos SDE PRO MAX, equipo de Santiago del Estero para el NASA Space Apps Challenge. Aplicamos Ciencia de Datos, IA (visión por computadora/agentes) y análisis geoespacial para resolver desafíos espaciales y terrestres con Open Data de la NASA.
summary:
Landing at the Moon’s South Pole is one of humanity’s greatest engineering puzzles. Because the Moon tilts at just 1.54 degrees and has no atmosphere, the Sun never climbs overhead; instead, it skims horizontally around jagged crater rims, leaving nearby crater floors in eternal, freezing darkness while Earth bobs low near the horizon. When launch delays occur, shifting a landing by just a few days can determine whether a lander thrives or loses power and Direct-to-Earth contact.

SDE PRO MAX — Lunar Pilot, created by Data Science and AI students from the Instituto Tecnológico Superior de Santiago del Estero (ITSE), bridges this gap by unifying NASA’s JPL Horizons ephemerides, LRO LOLA (240 m/px) elevation data, and LROC / Blue Marble imagery. Built with Java, Three.js, Python, and JSON—and accelerated with AI assistants—our interactive web platform transforms raw orbital and topographic data into 3D surface horizons, 360-degree terrain obstruction profiles, and 30-day side-by-side mission comparisons across six South Pole sites, empowering mission planners while inspiring students and educators.
details:
What It Does & How It WorksSDE PRO MAX — Lunar Pilot ([https://sdepromax.club](https://sdepromax.club)) is an interactive 3D lunar mission-planning web application designed to evaluate landing feasibility at the Moon’s South Pole. Using real NASA JPL Horizons astronomical ephemerides and LRO LOLA (240 m/px) laser altimetry, the platform computes the exact solar and Earth elevation angles over a 360-degree terrain obstruction horizon for six real candidate sites: Mons Mouton, Malapert Massif, Malapert A, Shackleton Crater, Shackleton–de Gerlache Ridge, and the Lunar South Pole. Users can scrub hour by hour across 30-day mission windows, monitor simulated solar power and battery reserves, inspect a 3D surface horizon rendered with LROC and NASA Blue Marble imagery, and run side-by-side Scenario A vs. B comparisons in Professional Mode to measure how launch delays affect illumination and Direct-to-Earth (DTE) radio windows.

Benefits

  • Unified Mission Trade-off Analysis: Replaces fragmented orbital tables and static elevation maps with a single real-time browser workspace.
  • Rapid Launch-Slip Assessment: Instantly quantifies how shifting a landing date by days or hours alters solar generation and Earth line-of-sight.
  • Accessible Dual-Mode Interface: Offers both an intuitive 3D exploratory view for students/educators and a quantitative A/B comparison dashboard for technical analysis.

Intended Impact Lunar Pilot democratizes mission engineering for NASA’s Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) and Artemis era. For researchers and mission designers, it serves as a fast prototyping and visualization tool for South Pole site selection. For students, teachers, and the public—starting from our community in Santiago del Estero, Argentina—it transforms abstract celestial mechanics into a tangible, visual experience that inspires interest in space science and data analysis.

Tools, Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • Languages & Web Technologies: Java, JavaScript, HTML5/CSS3, Three.js (WebGL 3D rendering), astronomy-engine, Python, and JSON.
  • NASA Data & Scientific Resources: NASA JPL Horizons System, LRO LOLA South Pole Digital Elevation Model (LDEM_75S_240M), LROC Color Mosaic, and NASA Blue Marble.
  • Development, Deployment & AI Assistance: Visual Studio Code, Git/GitHub, Netlify (sdepromax.club), Google Colab, and AI coding/design assistants (Google Gemini and Anthropic Claude) used to accelerate code refactoring, astronomical math verification, and bilingual documentation.
  • Hardware: Standard student laptops (Windows 11) running local development servers and browser-based WebGL simulations.

How Our Project Is Creative Instead of presenting cold numerical ephemeris tables, Lunar Pilot places the user directly on the lunar surface looking toward the horizon: watching the Sun skim jagged crater rims in real time while the Earth bobs above or dips behind distant mountains. Combining a 3D surface viewport, a 360° polar obstruction mask, an orbital terrain mesh, and side-by-side A/B mission comparison cards makes complex multi-variable orbital geometry immediately intuitive.

Factors Our Team Considered

  • Physical & Astronomical Realism: Accounting for the Moon’s 1.54° axial tilt, grazing solar incidence angles, terrain horizon masking up to 220 km, and Earth libration near the lunar horizon.
  • Scientific Transparency & Model Limits: Clearly documenting dataset resolution (240 m/px LOLA DEM), coordinate frames, and simulation assumptions so users understand both the precision and boundaries of the prototype.
  • Performance & Accessibility: Ensuring smooth 3D rendering directly in standard web browsers without requiring specialized desktop GIS software or paid licenses.
